title: A red wordmark and a great many spines
label: Brand gallery
lede: The wordmark, the site as it looked, and two freely licensed photographs of things FilmStruck was built on: Criterion’s shelf of editions and the TCM host who introduced its Hollywood classics. The drawings are our own.

archive.caption: The FilmStruck wordmark, with “FILM” in red.
archive.alt: The FilmStruck wordmark: a stylised F made of two bars, the word FILM in red and STRUCK in dark grey
archive.credit: FilmStruck wordmark, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:FilmStruck_logo.png), marked public domain there as a simple text logo. It remains a trademark of its owner.

archive.caption: The “Coming Soon” page, two days after the announcement.
archive.alt: The FilmStruck holding page of April 2016
archive.credit: Screenshot of an [Internet Archive capture](https://web.archive.org/web/20160428020642/http://filmstruck.com:80/) of filmstruck.com. Shown for commentary.

archive.caption: The home page five months after launch.
archive.alt: The FilmStruck home page of April 2017
archive.credit: Screenshot of an [Internet Archive capture](https://web.archive.org/web/20170418172151/https://www.filmstruck.com/) of filmstruck.com. Shown for commentary.

archive.caption: The Criterion Collection section of a Barnes & Noble store, photographed in January 2025. FilmStruck’s premium tier was a streaming version of this shelf.
archive.alt: Eight rows of wooden shelves filled with Criterion Collection Blu-ray and DVD cases, spines out

archive.caption: Ben Mankiewicz, the TCM host who recorded introductions for FilmStruck’s TCM Select, at the TCM Classic Film Festival in April 2025.[^12]

archive.credit: Photo: PrinceArchelaus, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ben_Mankiewicz_at_the_2025_TCM_Classic_Film_Festival.jpg), CC BY 4.0. Cropped only by resizing.
